newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -UK market volatility attracts FTSE trades.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -UK market volatility attracts FTSE trades.

text.p: A roller coaster day on the UK stock market brought attention to the FTSE 100 index options on Wednesday as traders either closed positions or took up new speculative positions ahead of Friday's May options expiry, dealers said.

In the latter category was the deal to buy 2,000 May 4750 calls at 5p. The trader is not expecting the FTSE to even remotely reach 4750 by expiry but is trying to take advantage of options volatility, gearing and the little time left to expiry in order to make a profit.
The deal will be profitable if the stock market manages to rise sufficiently and the percentage gain will be larger than if a longer-term option had been bought.
Other traders, believing the FTSE is now locked in a range, made spread trades. One such deal involved the sale of June 4575 puts at 43p as well as the purchase of 500 June 4325 puts at 6p.
As long as the FTSE stays above 4,575 by June expiry -- when both options will be worthless -- the trader will then collect a maximum of 27p.
At the close of business on the London stock market, the FTSE cash index was down 4.1 points at 4,686.9.

Over in stock options, the supermarket groups were active as the underlying stocks strengthened. The biggest deals were in Safeway where, in two separate deals, there were buyers of 500 July 360 calls at 7p.
And in pharmaceuticals group Glaxo Wellcome one trader expecting the shares to be volatile bought 200 July 1250 puts at 22p as well as 200 July 1300 calls at 35p in a long strangle strategy.
